# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute: my only working channel is gestures, and the only one who can read them is Deaf. Deaf in turn can speak — Blind hears speech, and so do I (my sheet forbids speaking, not hearing). So the only pipeline that exists is: manual (me) → gestures → Deaf → speech → Blind. Blind can get nothing from me directly; every cut instruction must travel through Deaf's voice.

What I hold is a light→wire table: green light → cut red, red light → cut yellow, yellow light → cut green. Deaf can see the light and the wire colours but has no way to know this table, and with zero shared symbols there is no way to just "read it out" cold — a colour has no gesture that names it. So round one cannot carry the table itself; it has to bootstrap a code. I send the most self-evident vocabulary I have, in order: a wave to mark this as deliberate signalling, thumbs up/down as yes/no, one-two-three on fingers as counting, then an open palm as "your move." That gives Deaf everything needed to do the smart thing: number the three colours (or ask me yes/no questions in batches), and next round I can answer with the three pairs as six gestures. I keep the payload minimal so nothing in it can be misread as table content.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "🫴"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, hands on the bomb. Inventory by touch: a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two, three. No colour and no printed mark reaches me, so every unknown on my board stays unknown to touch; the deciding facts are all visual or in your manual. My only possible action on this bomb is cutting a wire at position one, two, or three, and nothing else. If the manual uses the display or the light as a control, that path is impossible for me, so find the rule that picks a wire from what Deaf sees. Routing facts: I hear only Deaf's voice; you hear me and Deaf; Deaf hears nobody and sees every hand sign; I see no signs ever. Pipeline: you sign instructions to Deaf, Deaf speaks the decoded meaning aloud, I cut. Proposed code, using natural signs: finger count for wire numbers, thumb up for yes or cut, thumb down for no. I am signing hello then one, two, three to the room right now; those three signs should mean positions one, two, three from here on. Get Deaf to confirm the code out loud, since you can hear Deaf and Deaf cannot hear anyone. Never aim information at me through signs. This round, read the manual end to end and decide what you need from Deaf's eyes first.
Blind gestures: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Deaf says: Hello, this is Deaf. I can see the bomb and I cannot hear, so reach me only with gestures. Full report of what I see: the display reads zero. The light is green. There are three wires in order: wire one is yellow, wire two is green, wire three is red. Mute: I received your signs and I accept your code — thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three. Mute, remember Blind cannot see your gestures, so every instruction you have must come through me and I will speak it to Blind. Blind: I am your voice for Mute. Nobody act until Mute has matched the manual to this report.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The manual row that matters is settled: the light is green, and green means cut red. Deaf's report puts red at wire three, so the verdict is "cut wire three" — position three under Blind's fingers. Both other monkeys have already endorsed the same code from opposite sides: Blind proposed thumb-up = yes/cut and finger-counts for positions, and Deaf echoed it back to me in signs (👋👍☝✌🤟), which I can read. That's the rare moment where everything needed is already shared, so the safest move is to spend it immediately on the one instruction that matters, in the smallest, least misreadable form: attention wave, thumbs up, count to three. Deaf cannot hear any explanation, so the gesture string is the entire message — I add nothing that could dilute it. Deaf's job on receipt is to voice "cut wire three" to Blind, which Deaf has already committed to doing. I hold the rest of the table (red light → yellow, yellow light → green) in reserve until there's a colour vocabulary worth the round-trips; the light is green now and this row is what counts.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind speaking to you directly, Mute. I heard Deaf's full report, so you and I hold identical data: display reads zero, light is green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. Nothing more will ever appear on my board — everything left unknown to me is a colour or a printed mark, so the manual rule in your hands is the whole decision. Three protocol points. One: you cannot reach me directly, since you cannot speak and I cannot see signs. Your only path to me is through Deaf — sign your instruction to Deaf, and Deaf speaks it aloud, and I will hear Deaf's voice. Two: when you send the instruction, make it a single wire number in our code, finger count one, two, or three, so Deaf can relay it in one breath and I can act without decoding errors. Three: after every cut I make, Deaf must look again and report the display, the light, and all three wires aloud, because if the rule is iterative the state just reported dies the moment I cut. If the manual needs any visual detail beyond Deaf's report, query Deaf now. I am signing Deaf a thumbs-up right now meaning report received and standing by. I will not cut anything until your instruction arrives through Deaf's voice.
Deaf says: Both replies received. Mute, I see your signs: agreed, our number code is one, two, three. Blind, I saw your thumbs up — you cannot see any of these signs, so anything that concerns you I will always say out loud. Blind, here is the wire orientation: the wire I called one is the leftmost, two is the middle, three is the rightmost, on the bomb as it faces you. Please confirm by touch that you feel exactly three wires, and whether anything on it turns, clicks, or slides before we commit to any action. Mute, you heard my full report: display zero, light green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. You hold the manual. When you have found the matching rule, speak it directly to Blind next round — do not gesture it, Blind cannot see signs. If you need any more detail from the bomb — any label, marking, port, or the exact appearance of the display — gesture the item's number and then the pinched-fingers sign, 🤌, addressed to me, and I will answer aloud with everything visible. Until Mute speaks the instruction, nobody cuts, presses, or moves anything. Current status unchanged: display still zero, light still green.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 🤝]

Deaf misread my last transmission. I sent wave–yes–one–two–three meaning "yes: cut wire three," and Deaf parsed the count as mere confirmation of the number code. The manual verdict has not changed: light is green, green rows to red, red is wire three. So the payload is still "cut wire three" — it just has to land unambiguously this time. The failure mode was the run of all three numbers inviting an "enumeration" reading, so I strip it to a single number: attention wave, thumbs up (yes/cut, a code Deaf accepted aloud and Blind proposed), then three fingers alone. Three in isolation cannot be read as reciting the code; it can only be "the answer is three." Blind asked for exactly this form — a single wire number Deaf can relay in one breath.

Two corrections I must account for without being able to state them: Deaf asked me to "speak the instruction directly to Blind" — impossible, I have no voice, and my replying in gesture is itself the demonstration of that; the relay path stays me → signs → Deaf's voice → Blind, exactly as Blind mapped it. And I am deliberately deferring any colour vocabulary for later rows: stuffing a second payload (colour assignments) into this round risks Deaf merging it with the cut order, and a misread number on this channel is fatal. One message, one meaning. After Blind cuts, Deaf reports the new light, and only then do we build colour names if the table's next row is needed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👍", "🤟"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Answers to Deaf's questions, in the order Deaf asked them: yes, I feel exactly three wires. No, nothing turns, clicks, or slides. Full tactile inventory, complete: a display, a light, and three wires — position one leftmost, two middle, three rightmost as the bomb faces me — and nothing else. No buttons, no switches, no dials, no moving parts of any kind. The only operation this bomb accepts from my hands is cutting a wire at position one, two, or three, so if the manual's rule runs through the display or the light it is unusable by me; find the rule that selects a wire. Protocol revision so a discussion number can never be mistaken for an order: when you have the rule, sign Deaf the wire number followed by thumbs up — number then thumbs up means cut this wire, confirmed. A bare number is discussion only and Deaf must never relay it as an order. Deaf will read the pattern naturally: number, yes. Also, Deaf told you to speak the rule to me directly — that path does not exist, since you cannot speak and I cannot see signs. Keep the only working relay: you sign Deaf, Deaf speaks aloud, I cut. After every cut, Deaf re-reports the display, the light, and all three wires aloud before anything else happens. One assumption on record: I am treating Deaf's leftmost as my position one, since Deaf framed the orientation from the bomb facing me. No rule has reached me yet, so I cut nothing.
Deaf says: Status unchanged: display zero, light green, wire one yellow, wire two green, wire three red. Blind: I read your two signs as — yes, you feel exactly three wires; no, nothing turns, clicks, or slides. If that is wrong, correct me next round with signs to me: thumbs up or down, numbers. Keep answering me in signs, because I am deaf and never hear your voice — but do speak out loud toward Mute when you repeat instructions back, because Mute can hear you. Mute: I made an error earlier when I asked you to speak — you cannot speak, forget that. New plan, and since you can hear me, learn this code. Our standing signs remain: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one, two, three as numbers, pinched fingers means question or tell me details, closed fist means stop or hold, OK sign means ready. Now the letter code, one sign per letter, so you can spell any word from the manual to me: A is 🤚, B is 🖖, C is 🤏, D is 🫳, E is 🫴, F is 🫱, G is 🫲, H is 🫷, I is 🫸, J is 🤛, K is 🤜, L is 👊, M is 🖐, N is ✋, O is 🫰, P is 🤘, Q is 🤙, R is 👏, S is 🙌, T is 🫶, U is 👐, V is 🤲, W is 🤝, X is 🙏, Y is 🫵, Z is ✍. The raised hand with splayed little finger and thumb, 🤳, means a space between words, and the nail-polish sign, 💅, means end of message. Mute: next round, spell out first what your lone three meant, then the manual rule that matches this bomb — display zero, light green, wires yellow, green, red. Spell it letter by letter and I will voice it to Blind exactly as you wrote it. Blind: touch nothing until you hear me relay Mute's complete spelled instruction. When you do hear it, repeat it aloud word for word so Mute hears it and can confirm with thumbs up to me; only after that confirmation do you act.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 👌]

Deaf has finally built the bridge I needed: a full letter code, spoken aloud, which I could hear and can now use. This ends the ambiguity that killed my last two attempts — Deaf never parsed 👋👍🤟 as an order, and Blind's protocol (number *then* thumbs-up = cut order) was the reverse of what I sent. So this round I stop compressing and spell it out, exactly as requested. The payload: "CUT WIRE THREE" — light is green, green rows to red, red sits at position three. I encode the words in Deaf's letter code, then close with 🤟👍, which is Blind's own protocol shape: number three, then yes — the confirmed cut order, independent redundancy in case any letter is misread (the sensible parse "CUT WIRE THREE" also self-corrects against near-miss letters like I/H). The full table's other rows (red light → yellow wire one, yellow light → green wire two) stay in reserve: Deaf re-reports after every cut, so I will always get another round to spell the next row if the light ever changes, and a shorter message now is a safer one. Deaf voices this to Blind, Blind repeats it aloud, and I confirm with thumbs-up next round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🤏", "👐", "🫶", "🤳", "🤝", "🫸", "👏", "🫴", "🤳", "🫶", "🫷", "👏", "🫴", "🫴", "🤳", "🤟", "👍", "💅"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. I heard Deaf's whole plan and accept my part: I touch nothing, and when Deaf voices your spelled instruction I repeat it word for word aloud so you hear your own words come back. Compare them to what you signed: if exact, thumbs up to Deaf; if anything differs, make the stop sign. Now one gap to close, and you are my only route to close it, so sign this to Deaf: I can never see your confirmation, so Deaf must speak the confirmation aloud to me, in words like — Mute confirmed, cut wire N. I act only on Deaf's spoken voice. Until I hear the word cut together with a wire number from Deaf's mouth, my hands stay off. Second item for Deaf, also through you: the instruction must end in an explicit wire number, one, two, or three. If the manual rule is phrased in colours, Deaf must speak the translation out loud: yellow is position one, green is position two, red is position three. If time pressure ever appears, the compressed order format from my earlier message still stands: a number followed by thumbs up means cut that wire, and a bare number is never an order. Last thing: the board has been identical for three reports, display zero and steady green, so nothing we know of is counting down. Patience costs nothing yet; one wrong cut costs everything.
Deaf says: Mute's instruction is decoded and here it is, word for word: cut wire three. Blind, that means you: identify the wires by counting from the left edge of the bomb as it faces you — the leftmost wire is one, the middle is two, the third and rightmost is three. Wire three is the red one. Tool-cut wire three only. Nothing else — do not touch the display, the light, or the other two wires. Blind, before you act: repeat this instruction aloud now, word for word, so Mute can hear your repeat-back and verify it. Then wait — do not cut yet. Mute: I have relayed your instruction to Blind exactly as you spelled it. When you hear Blind repeat it back, gesture thumbs up to me if it is correct, thumbs down to me if anything is wrong, and I will voice the final go-ahead to Blind. Also, Mute: if the manual requires any further step, condition, or action after the cut, spell it to me the same way. If cutting wire three is the entire instruction, gesture the OK sign to me and nothing more. Status check: display zero, light green, all three wires intact.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 ✌ 👌]

I have verification in hand: Deaf voiced my instruction back word for word — "cut wire three" — and that matches the payload I spelled exactly. That is the check that matters, and I performed it with my own ears at source. Blind's repeat-back hasn't reached me yet, but turn order makes the strict sequence impossible anyway (my signs land after Blind's turn), and the repeat is only a third copy of content I have already verified twice. Holding my confirmation one more round would buy zero information and cost a full round. Deaf also asked two direct questions with a requested minimal answer format: is the decode correct (thumbs up), and is cutting wire three the entire instruction (OK sign, nothing more). Checking my manual: the green row is a single unconditional action — green light means cut red, red is position three on Blind's board, and no step, condition, or follow-up is attached to it. After the cut, Blind's standing protocol already forces Deaf to re-report display, light, and wires aloud; if the light has changed, I will spell the next row then. So nothing needs spelling now — the correct, safest reply is exactly the two signs Deaf requested and no more: thumbs up, confirmed; OK, this is the whole instruction, proceed. Deaf's own sign to me (👍 ✌ 👌) reads as receipt and readiness; its spoken relay was unambiguous, and speech is the operative channel to Blind, so nothing blocks the go-ahead.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | red |
| red | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind repeating Deaf's relay word for word for your verification: identify the wires by counting from the left edge of the bomb as it faces me — the leftmost wire is one, the middle is two, the third and rightmost is three. Wire three is the red one. Tool-cut wire three only. Nothing else — do not touch the display, the light, or the other two wires. Then wait — do not cut yet. End of repeat-back. Compare this to what you signed Deaf: if it is exact, thumbs up to Deaf; if anything differs, thumbs down or the stop sign. I will cut only when Deaf speaks the confirmation aloud to me — Mute confirmed, cut wire three. Until those words arrive in Deaf's voice, my hands are off the bomb. If your manual requires any further step or condition after the cut, or if cutting wire three is the entire instruction, you have already told Deaf how to signal that, and I will hear Deaf's voice either way. Standing by.
Deaf says: Blind — the instruction has been verified by Mute against the manual. You are cleared to act. Final command: cut wire three. That is the third wire counting from the left edge, the rightmost wire, the red one. Use the cutter and cut that one wire only. Do not touch wire one or wire two, the display, or the light. Cut it now. When it is done, answer me in signs: thumbs up to me if the bomb appears neutralized — display frozen, light off, no sound of any mechanism — thumbs down if anything changes for the worse. I will relay the outcome to Mute. That is all: one cut, wire three, rightmost, red.

The chain is closed and the order is in flight: Blind's repeat-back reached me word for word and matched my signed payload exactly (instruction, orientation, single-wire restriction, wait-clause — all identical), and Deaf has voiced the final command in Blind's only actionable channel. From my side there is nothing left to verify and nothing left to add — the correct row of my manual (green light → cut red → position three) is executing precisely as relayed.

Deliberately, I am not sending anything this round. Three reasons stand on where each receiver stands: Blind never sees signs, so nothing I gesture can help or hurt them mid-cut; Deaf does see signs, and an interjection landing during the cut risks being misread as a revision or a stop order — the worst possible noise at the decisive moment; and Deaf explicitly asked for OK "and nothing more" if cutting wire three is the entire instruction, which I already sent. If the light changes after the cut, Deaf's standing re-report protocol delivers the new state to me at the start of next round, and the letter code plus the compressed number-then-thumbs-up order format are both established — I can spell the next row (red light → cut yellow/wire one, yellow light → cut green/wire two) with no new setup. No timer has ever appeared on this bomb; one round of patience is free, one stray sign during the cut is not.

```
wait()
```
